review_status: draft v1 - shallow inshore drum profile

profile.size: Common 3-15 lb; bull reds over 30 lb
profile.swimming_depth: Shallow flats and channels; 0.3 to 15 m
profile.behavior: Forages over shallow oyster bars, seagrass flats, and muddy estuarine channels. Adult bull reds form fall spawning runs in inlet passes.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, favorable for foraging red drum.
factors.value_notes: The Florida Museum reports broad adult thermal tolerance around 4–34 °C; the NOAA-hosted habitat account reports captures across 36–92 °F, and the Gulf States Marine Fisheries Commission synthesis gives stage-specific temperature associations, including juvenile and egg/larval data. These support broad thermal biology, not a preferred adult South Florida SST curve. The configured 15–32 °C range and 22–28 °C ideal are not directly validated.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in shallow flats and channel habitat.
factors.value_notes: Sources document shallow estuarine nursery habitat, tidal creeks, oyster reefs, beaches, and adult movement into coastal/nearshore waters. This supports the general shallow coastal habitat role, but not a universal 0.3–15 m adult range or the 0.5–5 m ideal across life stages and seasons.

value_text.peak: It is peak fall red drum run season.
value_text.off: Outside peak fall run, but red drum are present year-round.

factors.value_notes: FWC acoustic-tagging research documents mature adults arriving in Florida Gulf nearshore spawning areas in late August and remaining through November; the Florida Museum reports spawning from mid-August to mid-November. This supports the fall spawning/migration context, but does not establish the configured August–December window or September–November peak as a catch-rate model, and timing differs among regions and populations.

text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.day: It is full daylight, when fish feed actively.

text.rising: The tide is rising, bringing in fresh water and bait.
text.falling: The tide is falling, flushing bait out through structure.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
